sources.reviewed_note: Rebased our stack onto upstream tag v0.10.0 (2026-09-11, 'Initial build for Deep North'), which is the tip of master - there are no commits after the tag. Read the delta as a whole rather than commit by commit: 2774 upstream commits since our old base 50d333d. One of our seven was dropped by the rebase as already upstream ('Remove unused using that breaks builds outside Visual Studio'), and one new one was needed: v0.10.0 targets release-day 1.0.0 and references UpscaledFrameBuffer.UpdateCurrentRenderScale and m_targetResolutionVertical, neither of which exists in 1.0.12, so the frame-scaling patch was removed. Filed as vhp-8mo.
sources.local_changes: Branch neuralyze/v0.10.0: seven commits on upstream v0.10.0. Six carried over from neuralyze/local (non-VR HarmonyPrepare guards, csproj SkipReleasePackaging condition, the BodyPose workaround, startup-stage reporting, name-based tracker role resolution, and the Mono/Linux plus no-base-assetbundle build fixes) and one new: 'Drop the frame-scaling patch Valheim 1.0 removed the target of'. The old neuralyze/local branch is left where it was as a record of what shipped before. Built on this host with scripts/build-valheimvr.sh against build/latest-1.0.12, a publicized 1.0.12 reference set - see build/README-1.0.12-refs.md, because the build cannot be reproduced against build/latest, which is the pre-1.0 client.
sources.published_note: GPL-3.0 source offer. Branch neuralyze/local pushed to the fork 2026-08-25 at 23f0ce4526cd and publicly reachable; the portal links it from the world page and from the release pages of releases carrying a flat_companion or vr_runtime (PORTAL_VHVR_SOURCE_URL). Correspondence is anchored per binary, not per release version, because release versions are the portal's and mean nothing upstream: each published ValheimVRMod.dll gets a tag shipped/valheimvrmod-<first 12 hex of its sha256> on the commit it was built from. Pushed so far: shipped/valheimvrmod-f879224e030c -> 23f0ce4526cd, the DLL inside vr-runtime-2.2.5-nospawnprobe.zip served as hrafnheim-vr 2.5.111 and doggerland/storgard/vangard-vr 2.5.36. mcs is not reproducible - two compiles of one tree differ in ~77800 of 600064 bytes - so a build is matched by size plus source markers, not by hash.
sources.correspondence_gap: Audited 2026-08-26 by hashing ValheimVRMod.dll inside all 1793 published zips under the artifact root. Seven distinct binaries are published and exactly one carries a shipped/ tag, so the previous claim that every published build is tagged was wrong about six of them; the offer text on the pages has been corrected to say what is true per binary. Two of the seven can never be given a tag: 3fe2ce08 (the Flat companion, 147 releases) and c2519916 (an earlier Flat companion, 2 releases). Each holds part of commit 1d6ea02 without the rest of it - both carry the two "Non-VR companion mode" literals that enter the history only at 1d6ea02, 3fe2ce08 lacks the HarmonyPrepare typeref added by 5ea5183 (an ancestor of 1d6ea02) and c2519916 has it, but neither has 1d6ea02's own LogDiagnostic - and no commit can hold a descendant's strings without its ancestor's, nor half of a single commit. The cause is that the seven commits were authored on 2026-08-18 by grouping finished changes into themed commits rather than replaying how the tree evolved: the non-VR branch was written by 07-26 and HarmonyPrepare and LogDiagnostic by 07-28, but they were committed in the opposite order, so builds taken from the tree in between fall between the commits. Correcting an earlier note: the reflog does not start 2026-08-18, it starts 2026-07-26 04:15:44 with the clone of upstream at a10f24fc - 43 minutes before 3fe2ce08 was compiled - and it still does not help, because the intermediate tree was never committed. Searched and not found: no commit, no stash, no dangling object (the four dangling blobs are the vhvr-0.9.21*.zip archives), and no second copy of the source - a find for ValheimVRMod.cs across every mounted big drive returns exactly one checkout. Closing those two therefore needs a rebuild from a commit on the branch and a republish, which is a deliberate publish decision and not a repo change; until then the offer names both binaries and says we cannot name their revision, which is the honest state rather than a discharged-looking one.

sources.why: The container the world operation scripts drive. valheim_provision.py reads its default.env for the PGID a world's mounts are chowned to.
sources.reviewed_note: Read all 18 commits and the 14 files they touch. Material to us: Debian 12 then 13 base-image upgrades with 32-bit glibc restored, busybox cron replacing Debian vixie-cron, a UMASK calculation change that would land on the world directories provisioning chowns, and secrets support. The libdoorstop env-var rename (DOORSTOP_ENABLED/DOORSTOP_TARGET_ASSEMBLY) is already in our tree: our local commit 3ad0632 made the same fix independently, so upgrading converges and that part of our patch can be dropped. Upgrade deferred to a maintenance window because it replaces the base image under four live worlds; filed as a bead.
sources.local_changes: Four local commits, none of them upstream, published to https://github.com/neuralyze/valheim-server-docker branch neuralyze/local (we have no push access to community-valheim-tools, so that fork is the only off-host copy): 40252fce 'Update local Valheim server runtime', 3f736897 'Apply directory permissions to Valheim 1.0 world directories', 43844851 'Sync BepInEx patchers so preloader patches survive a rebuild', and f000f97f 'Never sync the download cache over the install when the update failed'. The last one is load-bearing: valheim-updater's download-failure branch logged "an existing version was found locally - using it" and then fell through to 'rsync -a --delete dl/ server/', which overwrote a correct 1.0.12 install with a stale 0.221.12 cache and reported it as "already the latest version". That silently downgraded three worlds on 2026-09-13 and emptied their saves - see bead vhp-oxn. Note also that docker-compose.yaml carries uncommitted operator changes (CONFIG_DIR/DATA_DIR made required rather than defaulting to a shared directory, WEBMAP_PORT dropped); those are deliberate and predate this session.

sources.why: Server-side character storage, and the mechanism this fleet uses to hand out tiered kits and skills. TEMPORARY SITUATION, changed 2026-09-14: we now compile this mod ourselves from unmodified upstream source and install that build on the Ulfsland server and on the clients of its four editions. Nothing of it is committed to this repository and nothing of it is published outside the operator's own machines. Listed here because it is third-party code that reaches players through us, and because both the licence position and the reason this is temporary have to be written down rather than rediscovered.
sources.source_index: our own build of upstream source; see build_note. The Hexium route (index_api below) is still implemented in tools/valheim_mods.py and cmd/profile-definition-builder but is no longer used for this package.
sources.artifact_sha256_note: OUR build of bb7d3cd6: ServerCharacters.dll as compiled by tools/servercharacters/build.sh. Reproducible - two independent runs produced these bytes. For reference, the author's own 1.4.17 DLL is 0b497b7e830365bc57d0a5ada200e9e571b0f3e3625ac08de06a2bc528850872 inside archive 7f17f1164579bf58c8fce1408e2b2471e64ef98961fd91f382a208f4d04b187f on Hexium; we do not ship those bytes.
sources.archive_sha256_note: The Thunderstore-shaped archive built around that DLL with a manifest.json of our own, 482416 bytes, byte-reproducible. This is the SHA256 the four ulfsland-* profile definitions published at 1.0.10 carry for Smoothbrain-ServerCharacters, and the digest cmd/valheim-profile-sync checks the copy embedded in itself against.
sources.reviewed_note: Thunderstore's newest is 1.4.16 (2025-05-02) and it MUST NEVER be installed on Valheim 1.0.12: PlayerProfile.GetCharacterFolderPath moved to SaveSystem, so ServerCharacters.Initialize throws MissingMethodException at FejdStartup.Awake and the mod never initialises - while the Harmony patches on PlayerProfile.LoadPlayerFromDisk, Player.Load, Skills.Load and Inventory.Load are already installed, leaving live save/load patches over an uninitialised profile store. Seven further members are unresolvable against 1.0.12's assembly_valheim; all eight are fixed by upstream commit bb7d3cd6 ('fix for deep north', 2026-09-09), which is 1.4.17. Verified by resolving every type and member reference in the shipped binary against the running server's assemblies: 486/488 typerefs and 5159/5178 memberrefs resolve, and the unresolved remainder is byte-for-byte the same set as in an independent from-source build of bb7d3cd6 - System.Numerics.Vector intrinsics plus one ImmutableArray span overload, both supplied by Unity's BCL at runtime. Details in tools/servercharacters/README.md.
sources.local_changes: No source changes. The mod is compiled from upstream bb7d3cd6 exactly as published - no patches, no retargeting, and no publicizing beyond the publicized GAME assemblies upstream's own build expects. Three support files under tools/servercharacters exist only because upstream's build cannot run on this host and are not part of the mod: ServerCharacters.csproj (upstream's wants a NuGet packages/ tree and hand-publicized assemblies), publicize.cs, and Request.cs, which upstream generates from Request.proto with protogen - a .NET tool this build cannot run - and whose members were read back out of the shipped assembly with Cecil and reproduced exactly.
sources.build_note: tools/servercharacters/build.sh clones bb7d3cd6 into a temp directory, compiles it in a throwaway dotnet/sdk:8.0 container, ILRepacks it, and writes internal/servercharacters/embedded/ServerCharacters.zip. That path is GITIGNORED: the archive is built or placed locally and never committed, because this repository is published and committing an unlicensed third-party binary is the difference between the operator's private choice about their own machines and public redistribution. internal/servercharacters embeds whatever is at that path; the client and the definition builder both read it from there, so the bytes a client writes and the SHA256 a definition publishes cannot disagree.
sources.authorisation: The operator instructed this on 2026-09-14, for their own server and their own player group, knowing the licence position: 'go ahead and use servercharacters 1.4.17 for now because it will get updated on thunderstore soon and we will fix the legal issue in the next couple days', and, when asked which delivery route, 'i didnt say use the hexium path.. i mean the compile from source'. It applies to Ulfsland only - the four ulfsland-* profiles - and to no shared profile, so no Hrafnheim, Doggerland, Storgard or Vangard client receives it.
sources.redistribution: The licence facts are unchanged and are why this is temporary: the repository has no LICENSE file, so it is all rights reserved, and on 2026-09-11 the author refused a public request (issue #98, 'Fork and LICENSE') to fork and redistribute a modified build - 'No, sorry. Especially not on Thunderstore.' What we do now is narrower than that request and is still not something to extend: we publish no copy anywhere public, commit no copy, and host no copy on the portal's own pages; the bytes travel only from this host to the operator's own clients, inside the client executable they download from the operator's own portal. Do NOT commit the binary, publish it to Thunderstore or any index, offer it on a public page, or ship it to any world outside Ulfsland. If the situation outlives the operator's 'next couple of days', it needs the author's permission or removal.
sources.operational_risk: Version skew is gone by construction: the server plugin and every client's embedded copy come from one archive, so ServerSync's MinimumRequiredVersion 1.4.17 / ModRequired true cannot be unsatisfiable. What replaces it is a build dependency - a publish from a tree whose archive is missing fails naming tools/servercharacters/build.sh, and a client built from a tree with a DIFFERENT archive refuses the install with a message telling the player to download the current client rather than joining with a mismatched assembly.
sources.retire_when:
The author publishes 1.4.17 or later to Thunderstore, or we stop using the mod. Then: `valheim_mods.py --profile

add Smoothbrain-ServerCharacters` replaces the whole arrangement, and every block marked 'TEMPORARY: local ServerCharacters build' comes out - internal/servercharacters and its embedded/ directory, the local-build branches in cmd/profile-definition-builder and cmd/valheim-profile-sync (including cmd/valheim-profile-sync/servercharacters_package.go and its test), LOCAL_BUILD_PACKAGES and local_build_package in tools/valheim_mods.py, and the .gitignore entry. The Hexium backend stays: it is the mechanism for the next mod that lives off Thunderstore.
sources.checkout_note: Not a checkout of the upstream repository - we keep none. build.sh clones bb7d3cd6 on demand into a temp directory and deletes it. The only artifact retained is the gitignored archive under internal/servercharacters/embedded/.
